subject: adr
summary: The Alternate Dispute Resolution exam paper exhibits a strong historical focus on core arbitration topics, particularly arbitration agreements, the appointment and termination of arbitrators, and the grounds for setting aside arbitral awards. Questions are consistently structured into two distinct formats: Part A short notes (traditionally valued around 6 marks) and Part B detailed essay questions (typically valued around 16 marks). Beyond arbitration, topics concerning conciliation, foreign awards enforcement, Section 89 of the CPC, and Family Courts appear with regular frequency in long-answer sections. Overall, the paper heavily emphasizes statutory mechanisms under the 1996 Act and judicial integration of ADR.
